sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record for Wui [wuii1234] (comment: recently discovered language in Wui village, previously counted as Patsho Khiamniungan [kix]; unintelligible to all neighbouring languages; sole reference Coupe 2023; 0 descriptive refs).
Wikipedia (English), 'Wui language' (created 2023-10-18 by user Lingnanhua directly from Coupe's ICSTLL56 paper and its supplementary Swadesh list; revid 1330718383).
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Second-hand report of Coupe (2023): consonant and vowel inventories, and 'There are three phonemic tones in Wui, which are: high level /55/, mid level /33/, high falling /52/'; every lexical item and pronoun is transcribed with a Chao tone number per syllable (e.g. tʰa³³ɲu³³lia⁵² 'woman'), i.e. a syllable-tone language.

sources.citation: Coupe, Alexander R. 2023. Preliminary Report on Wui: An Undocumented Language of Eastern Nagaland. Paper presented at ICSTLL56, 10-12 Oct 2023, Chulalongkorn University, Bangkok. 23 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The ONLY description of Wui in existence (Glottolog's sole reference; source of the Wikipedia phoneme/tone inventory). Its phonology section will state the tone system and, if anywhere, whether there is word stress or a fixed prominence position (Central Naga relatives such as Mongsen Ao are described by Coupe as tonal with no contrastive stress). Copy exists in Hammarström's collection as eurasia/; otherwise request from the author (arcoupe@ntu.edu.sg, Emeritus Assoc. Prof., NTU Singapore).

tone.quote: This paper presents a preliminary overview of a newly discovered Tibeto-Burman language known by the endonym [tʰa³³weɪ⁵² ma³³lan³¹]. It is spoken in Wui, a village of approximately 150 houses located 10km west of the international border on the Patsho Range in eastern Nagaland’s Noklak District (26.036N, 95.067E). [...] A preliminary analysis of phonology and word formation patterns instead suggests that Wui is more closely related to the Aoic cluster, even though it lacks a rhotic, which is otherwise one of the defining characteristics of Aoic.
tone.locator: Abstract book ICSTLL-56, p. 13 as printed, abstract 'Preliminary Report on Wui', paragraphs 1-2
tone.says: No tone inventory is stated in the abstract. It transcribes the endonym with Chao pitch numerals on every syllable ([tʰa³³weɪ⁵² ma³³lan³¹]: mid level 33, high falling 52, low falling 31), i.e. the author treats Wui as a syllable-tone language, and says the paper presents 'a preliminary analysis of phonology and word formation patterns'. The explicit statement (three phonemic tones: high level 55, mid level 33, high falling 52) is known only second-hand from the Wikipedia digest of the full pape…
